THE 
MONTREAL 
YMCA 


OUR MISSION 


“The Montreal YMCA is a partnership 
of volunteers and staff committed to the 
fulfilment of people in spirit, mind and 
body, and to the development of self- 
reliance in the individual and the 
community. 


Through its actions, programs and 
services, the Montreal YMCA will 
reflect the needs and aspirations of the 
community and will work with 
individuals, local communities and 
communities in developing countries in 
achieving social justice and control of 
their environments”. 


Concordia 1984 


Standing from left to right: Chris Ferguson, Bernard Matte, John Hall, Vianney Bélanger. 
Brian Benedetti, Rita Vaillancourt, Suzanne Aboud. 


Sitting down: Victor M. Drury, Sol Kasimer. 
Regrets: Deborah Bonney, Len Liben, Pierre Riverin. 


The Montreal YMCA has had another extraordinary year. We have now completed year 
one of a three-year strategic plan, a year that saw us embark on strategies for programs, 
finance, facilities, fund-raising, human resources and public image. 


We successfully launched our much needed $13 million, five-year Capital Development 
Campaign. 

For the first time in our 134 year history, we had 100% participation of the members 
of the Metropolitan Board of Directors and the members of the Senior Management 
Group. All 39 Board members and 26 members of the Management Group took part 
in this year’s Sustaining Membership Campaign. 

We signed an offer to lease a 28,000 square foot physical fitness center in the 
Complexe Guy-Favreau. The center, we expect, will open as a YMCA Branch in June 
1986. 

Job Generation, the Y’s National Program for unemployed youth, coordinated through 
the Montreal YMCA, became operational in ten centers across the country. 

We established a Spirit Task Force to explore ways of addressing that part of our 
Mission which seeks to “fulfill individuals in SPIRIT”. 

We presented Rosalie Williams Sinclair — great grand-daughter of Sir George 
Williams, founder of the YMCA — with a recording of a speech given by her great 
grandfather in 1894 to students at Springfield College, Massachusetts. 

Our Justice Initiatives Program was honoured by La Société de Criminologie du 
Québec with the Denis Gagné Award for outstanding work in the prevention of 
juvenile delinquency. 

We created a new logo as part of our ongoing campaign to upgrade the YMCA’s public 
image. The logo was designed to reflect both the excellence, and the pioneering and 
innovative nature of the Association. 

We had an operating surplus for the third year in a row. 


We are optimistic about the future. Our optimism is based on the great wealth of talent 
we have in our volunteers and staff and their firm commitment to the Y. 


cto 3 ed Nga 


Solomon Kasimer 
Director General 


Victor M. Drury F 
President 


PROGRAMS 
AND 
ACTIVITIES 


The YMCA is a whole world waiting to 
be discovered through its high quality 
physical activity programs offered by 
recognized professionals. Whether in the 
gym or pool, alone or in a group, the 
person who uses the YMCA facilities is 
taking part in programs that honor a long 
tradition of well-being. 


Physical fitness, jogging, weight-training, 
aquatic activities, back care, post-cardiac 
rehabilitation, aerobic dance, classical 
and jazz ballet, team sports, racquet 
sports, martial arts. 


Children enjoy an environment that is 
both pleasant and conducive to positive, 
personal development in the physical and 
emotional sense. 


— Programs for preschool children, 
after-school programs, day camp 
(summer-time), day-care, home day- 
care services, recreation for 
handicapped children. 


Located near Saint-Sauveur in a beautiful 
natural setting, Kamp Kanawana has been 
offering outdoor adventure to young 
people, ages 6 to 18, for the past 75 
years. Group living, open-air activities 
and shared responsibility make each 
summer season an unforgettable one for 
our young campers. 


Ww 


At the present time, the Montreal YMCA’s community programs focus on three major 
themes: unemployment, especially among young adults, minority groups and their 
participation in society and the quality of life in Montreal neighbourhoods. 


The Montreal YMCA makes its presence felt in the community through various 
initiatives, including employment and housing co-ops, unemployed youth committees, 
assistance to single-parent families, urban development, public housing, green space, air 
quality and pedestrian safety. 


The Community Justice Initiatives Office 
helps young people in conflict, young 
offenders and early-school leavers, 
through its progressive and well- 
established programming. Our social 
reintegration program and employment 
and manpower services for ex-inmates 
are other activities undertaken by an 
organization dedicated to the total 
development of the individual. 


Résidence 


= 


Language and computer courses, 
continuing education and residence 
services for refugees and travelers 
complete the broad spectrum of programs 
and services provided by the Montreal 
YMCA.

The YMCA seeks to enable all peoples 
of the world to achieve social justice and 
control their own development. 


Our international development programs 
make Montrealers aware of the situation 
in Third-World countries and support 

development projects in these countries.

MESSAGE OF 

THE CHAIRMAN 

OF THE MONTREAL 
YMCA FOUNDATION 


~~ 


The mandate of the Montreal YMCA Foundation, set up on August 10th, 1983, is: 


© To solicit, by all appropriate means, and receive all donations, contributions, bequests 
and subscriptions of a charitable nature, in kind or in cash, for the exclusive 
advantage and use of ‘“‘The Young Men’s Christian Association of Montreal’’. 


¢ To these ends, to acquire, retain, administer, invest and reinvest these donations, 
contributions, bequests and subscriptions free of charge and channel these funds, with 
the exception of those needed to cover the administration costs of the corporation, 
exclusively to the ‘*Young Men’s Christian Association of Montreal’’. 


During the year the Foundation directors organized and launched the Montreal YMCA 
Capital Development Campaign. Ghislain Hawey and John Churchill-Smith are the Co- 
Chairmen of the overall campaign and twelve well-known Montrealers have agreed to 

act as honorary patrons. They are: 


Jane H. Dunn, Alphonsine Howlett, Louise B. Vaillancourt. 


G. Drummond Birks, Charles L. Bronfman, H. Roy Crabtree, David M. Culver, A. 
Jean de Grandpré, Paul G. Desmarais, Ronald H. Perowne, William I.M. Turner 
and Jack H. Warren. 


The Montreal YMCA needs $13,000,000 for buildings and improvements. Thirteen 
million dollars — a considerable sum, no doubt. But not all that much when one 
considers the Montreal YMCA’s urgent needs over the next five years for the repair and 
development of its facilities better to meet the continuing needs of its thousands of users 
throughout the Montreal area. 

At year-end, May 31st, 1985, our fund-raising committee is pleased to announce that a 

total of $1,300,000 had been received in donations and pledges. Moreover, I would like 

to bring to your attention the important efforts of the many volunteers involved in our 
fund-raising programs, without whose dedication and enthusiasm we could not have 
reached 10% of our overall financial goal only four months after the start of the 
campaign. 

Of the $1,700,000 target from governments during the Capital Development Campaign, 

the Montreal YMCA Foundation has raised $260,367 to date. Due to provincial 

government regulations regarding allocation of capital funding, the amount has been paid 
directly to the Montreal YMCA and consequently is not, as such, reflected in the 
financial statements of the Foundation, which therefore understate by that amount the 
apparent success of the Campaign. This is purely an accounting matter and the 
arrangements between the Y and the Foundation are such that the Foundation’s capacity 
to discharge its responsibilities is not affected. 

P.S.: At the time of the meeting (85-09-24), $1,700,000 have been received in 
donations and pledges on the overall target of $7,700,000. As for the YMCA 
Resources’ and Governments’ level, more than $1,450,000 have been received in 
donations and pledges on the overall target of $5,300,000. 


Jack H. Warren O.C. 


After two years as Director General of 
the Montreal YMCA Foundation, it gives 
me great pleasure to announce the 
progress made in our four major fund- 
raising programs. This year the 
Sustaining Membership Campaign was 
held for the second time and the three 
other programs made their debut. 


Cumann Abana. Rornar Mille And -Dise 
Suzanne Aboud, Bernard Matte and Va 


Sustaining Membership Program 


During the year 1984-1985, the 
Foundation raised $91,312 from the 
contributions of 712 donors, compared to 
$81,100 and 660 donors in 1983-1984. 
The Co-Chairmen of the Sustaining 
Membership Program, Victor M. Drury 
and Brian Marcil, along with their 
superb team of governors and honorary 
patrons, who helped make this second 
year a success, would like to express 
their gratitude to our 712 sustaining 
members for their generous donations. 


The overall financial target of the 
sustaining Membership Program is 

$ 750,000 for the period 1984-1989. The 
program centers on past and present 
YMCA committee members and 
employees, as well as friends of the 
Montreal YMCA. 


Members and Participants Program 


Claude Lemay and Victor M. Drury 
were the two Co-Chairmen of our 1985 
Members and Participants Fund-Raising 
Campaign. With their assistance, $39,160 
was raised from among 1,207 donors. 


The total financial objective of the 
Members and Participants Program is 
$500,000 for the period 1985-1989. This 
fund-raising campaign is held once 
yearly during February and March and 
all monies raised from it will be used 
exclusively to repair the buildings and 
replace equipment at our branches and 
Kamp Kanawana as planned in the 
Montreal YMCA’s facilities development 
program. 


Endowment and Bequest Program 
and the Heritage Club 


Maurice Massé, President of Timminco, 
brought together a group of long-time 
friends of the YMCA to form the 
Endowment and Bequest Committee. The 
Committee seeks to establish a major 
fund to ensure a solid financial base for 
the Montreal YMCA founded in 1851. 


First training session for branch leaders. 
The Heritage Club is a special group of men and women who believe in the purposes 
and traditions of the Y and wish to ensure that this Heritage is continued for future 


generations. 


Members of the Heritage Club have included the Montreal YMCA in their estate 
planning either by will, insurance, immediate gift or by creating a special trust. As this 
fellowship grows, the Y will be able to build in long-range financial stability and remain 
a powerful force for good in our community. 


Jean Béliveau, Sylvie Bernier, Claire Pimparé and George Springate. 


Gifts to the Montreal YMCA may be designated for its general purposes, or may be 
restricted to specific branches, programs, or such continuing needs as camp scholarships, 
youth work, leadership development, capital construction, site acquisition, or a broad 
range of other interests. Memorial gifts in any amount, are always welcomed by the 
YMCA Endowment Fund. 


So far, the Endowment Fund Committee has received: 


2 Bequests $ 42,000 
9 Immediate gifts $ 7,965 
1 Insurance policy — value $ 5,000 
9 Confirmed bequests $337,000 
5 Confirmed bequests 
(no amount indicated) 
* 5 Signed “letters of intent” 

$391,965 


* Individuals who have indicated that they will be making a 
provision in their will, but have not yet confirmed that this 
has been done. 


Corporations, Foundations 
and Special Names Program 


John Churchill-Smith and Ghislain 
Hawey are the Co-Chairmen of the 
YMCA’s Corporations, Foundations and 
Special Names Fund-Raising Campaign. 
They are seconded by Walter Light, 
former Chairman of Northern Telecom, 
Philip O’Brien, President of the Montreal 
Chamber of Commerce and Devencore 
Inc., and Louis Paul Nolet, Chairman of 
Dometal Inc. 


This program consists of four divisions: 


¢ The Lead Gifts Division, comprising 
28 corporations and foundations, 
held from January | to June 30, 1985. 

¢ The Major Gifts Division, made up of 
132 corporations and foundations, 
running from September | to 
December 31, 1985. 

e The Thousand Plus Division, 
encompassing 525 corporations, to be 
held from January | to June 30, 1986. 

e The Ethnic Groups Division, 
to be held from September 1 to 
December 31, 1986. 


To date, the Corporations, Foundations 
and Special Names Program has received 
more than $965,500 in donations and 
pledges, which constitutes 12.5% of the 
overall target for this campaign of 
$7,700,000. Furthermore, no less than 250 
volunteers from the business world are 
lending their valuable assistance as we 
approach these organizations. Our 


sincerest thanks. 
VA 


Jean-Robert Nolet

SUSTAINING 
MEMBERSHIP 
PROGRAM 


The Young Men’s Christian Association of the Montreal Area expresses its appreciation 
to the hundreds of people who became Sustaining Members during the 1984-1985 
campaign run by the Montreal YMCA Foundation. Proceeds from sustaining 
memberships are used towards the building repair and equipment replacement program 
and also to the financial support of international programs. 


Under the leadership of Victor M. Drury and Brian Marcil, the Foundation received 
gifts from more than 723 donors. To those persons who contributed, the Foundation owes 


special appreciation.

For 134 years the YMCA has served the people of the Montreal area. However, length of 
time in itself does not assure the quality or value of an institution. One valid test for any 
public-service organization such as the YMCA is the number of young people whose 
attitudes and values are formed through participation in the YMCA movement, and who 
are today in significant positions of leadership in their businesses, professions, churches 
and communities. 


A second test is the evidence that many parents seek the YMCA as a partner in the 
challenging vocation of child development. 


One goal of the Montreal YMCA can be stated clearly and concisely to assist every 
individual in developing his total personality in order to achieve his full potential in 
relationship to himself, his fellows and his God. 


To realize such a goal, the people of the Montreal area have given of their time, talents, 
and resources over the years, certain that an investment in young people pays increasing 
dividends. As individuals they have extended their lives and influence into the future by 
supporting a proven, purposeful institution - the Montreal Young Men’s Christian 
Association. 


It is the privilege of the Montreal Association to recognize and thank those who have 
made gifts or indicated bequests to its endowment fund. We welcome them as members 
of the Heritage Club of the Montreal YMCA Foundation.
